title: Completeness comparison of equivalence fibers with object paths
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, internal functor simplicial sets, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], Kan fibrations from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and complete Segal spaces from [def-coef-segal-space]. Let $W$ be a complete Segal space, put $A=W_0$ and $p_W=(d_1,d_0):W_{\mathrm{eq}}\to A^2$. For vertices $x,y$ of $A$, let $E_W(x,y)$ be the union of the isomorphism components in the strict mapping fiber $M_W(x,y)$, using the homotopy category of [lem-coef-segal-homotopy-category-components]. Put $K_A=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,A)$, $q_A=(\operatorname{ev}_0,\operatorname{ev}_1):K_A\to A^2$, and let $c_A:A\to K_A$ insert constant paths. Write $\Delta_A:A\to A^2$ for the diagonal and $\operatorname{Path}_A(x,y)=\operatorname{fib}_{(x,y)}q_A$.

There is a zigzag of weak homotopy equivalences
$$E_W(x,y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{(x,y)}p_W\longleftarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{(x,y)}\Delta_A\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{(x,y)}q_A\longleftarrow\operatorname{Path}_A(x,y).$$
The outer arrows insert constant base paths; the inner arrows are induced on the specified path-model homotopy fibers by $s_0:A\to W_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $c_A$, respectively, over $A^2$. For every map $f:W\to W'$ of complete Segal spaces, the maps $f_0,f_1$, and postcomposition by $f_0$ on paths induce a commuting map of these zigzags at $(x,y)$ and $(f_0x,f_0y)$, retaining every simplex. For $x=y$ each arrow preserves the points represented by the identity arrow, the vertex $x$ with its constant base path, and the constant loop $c_A(x)$, as applicable. No nonemptiness of off-diagonal fibers is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, implications (1)⇒(4), diagram (6.3), with the homotopy-fiber replacements made explicit.

proof.text: By Reedy fibrancy, $A=W_0$ and $W_1$ are Kan complexes. In outer degree one the matching object is $A\times A$: its two indexing maps are the two endpoints and there are no nonidentity arrows between them. Thus the matching map is $e_W=(d_1,d_0):W_1\to A^2$, a Kan fibration. Products of Kan complexes are Kan by filling a horn in each factor. Apply the component-restriction lemma to $e_W$, with the subset of components defining $W_{\mathrm{eq}}$ in the source and every component in the target. It makes $W_{\mathrm{eq}}$ Kan and $p_W$ a Kan fibration. The homotopy-category-components lemma identifies its strict fiber at $(x,y)$ with exactly $E_W(x,y)$, including every simplex, not merely the vertices.

source.place: Rezk, diagram (6.3) and Proposition 6.4, printed pp. 14-15; explicit path-model expansion by the worker.

proof.text: Apply the internal-hom corner-map lemma to $\partial\Delta^1=\{0\}\amalg\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and $A\to\Delta^0$. Its corner map is $q_A:K_A\to A^2$, since a map out of the two discrete endpoints is precisely a pair of simplices of $A$. Hence $q_A$ is a Kan fibration. The same lemma with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ makes $K_A$ Kan. Apply path-space fibration replacement to $\mathrm{id}_A:A\to A$. The resulting $E_{\mathrm{id}_A}=A\times_{A,\mathrm{ev}_0}K_A$ is canonically isomorphic to $K_A$, by $(a,\gamma)\mapsto\gamma$ with inverse $\gamma\mapsto(\mathrm{ev}_0\gamma,\gamma)$. Under this isomorphism its weak equivalence $i:A\to E_{\mathrm{id}_A}$ is precisely $c_A$. Thus $c_A$ is a weak equivalence and $q_Ac_A=\Delta_A$. Completeness gives a weak equivalence $s_0:A\to W_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and the simplicial identities give $p_Ws_0=\Delta_A$.

source.place: Rezk, diagram (6.3) and Proposition 6.4, printed pp. 14-15; explicit path-model expansion by the worker.

proof.text: Put $B=A^2$ and $b=(x,y)$. For any map $r:Z\to B$ write its specified homotopy fiber as pairs $(z,\gamma)$, where $\gamma:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to B$ starts at $r(z)$ and ends at the constant $n$-simplex $b$. Apply the Kan-pullback-path comparison with $(u,v)=(p_W:\!W_{\mathrm{eq}}\to B,\,b:\!\Delta^0\to B)$. Its strict pullback is $E_W(x,y)$ by step 1 and its path pullback is $\operatorname{hofib}_b p_W$. Since $p_W$ is a Kan fibration, the map $a\mapsto(a,c_B(b))$ is a weak equivalence. Apply the same lemma with $(u,v)=(q_A,b)$. Its strict pullback is $\operatorname{Path}_A(x,y)$ and its path pullback is $\operatorname{hofib}_b q_A$; the map $\alpha\mapsto(\alpha,c_B(b))$ is a weak equivalence since $q_A$ is a Kan fibration. The cited lemma also ensures these path-model fibers are Kan complexes.

source.place: Rezk, diagram (6.3) and Proposition 6.4, printed pp. 14-15; explicit path-model expansion by the worker.

proof.text: Apply homotopy-pullback invariance to the cospans $A\xrightarrow{\Delta_A}B\xleftarrow{b}\Delta^0$ and $W_{\mathrm{eq}}\xrightarrow{p_W}B\xleftarrow{b}\Delta^0$, with comparison maps $(s_0,\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^0},\mathrm{id}_B)$. Their objects are Kan by steps 1-2, the squares commute by $p_Ws_0=\Delta_A$, and all three comparison maps are weak equivalences. The induced weak equivalence is exactly $(a,\gamma)\mapsto(s_0a,\gamma)$ from $\operatorname{hofib}_b\Delta_A$ to $\operatorname{hofib}_b p_W$. Apply the same lemma to the latter source cospan and $K_A\xrightarrow{q_A}B\xleftarrow{b}\Delta^0$, using $(c_A,\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^0},\mathrm{id}_B)$. This gives the weak equivalence $(a,\gamma)\mapsto(c_Aa,\gamma)$ to $\operatorname{hofib}_b q_A$. Together with step 3 these are the four arrows in the asserted directions.

source.place: Rezk, diagram (6.3) and Proposition 6.4, printed pp. 14-15; explicit path-model expansion by the worker.

proof.text: For a map $f:W\to W'$, the induced homotopy-category functor preserves isomorphisms. The component lemma therefore makes $f_1$ restrict to $W_{\mathrm{eq}}\to W'_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Put $v=f_0\times f_0:B\to B'$. On the homotopy fibers the three vertical maps are respectively $(a,\gamma)\mapsto(f_1a,v\gamma)$, $(a,\gamma)\mapsto(f_0a,v\gamma)$, and $(\alpha,\gamma)\mapsto(f_0\alpha,v\gamma)$; on the strict fibers they are $a\mapsto f_1a$ and $\alpha\mapsto f_0\alpha$. These are simplicial maps because restriction commutes with postcomposition in every degree. For the two inner arrows their commutation follows respectively from $f_1s_0=s_0f_0$ and $f_0c_A(a)=c_{A'}(f_0a)$; for the outer arrows it follows from $v c_B(b)=c_{B'}(v b)$. These equations hold for parameterized simplices, so the whole zigzag commutes strictly. If $x=y$, its distinguished elements, in order from left to right, are $s_0x$, $(s_0x,c_B(x,x))$, $(x,c_B(x,x))$, $(c_A(x),c_B(x,x))$, and $c_A(x)$, and the four formulas send them to one another. Nothing chooses a point in an off-diagonal fiber. If $A$ is empty there are no pairs of vertices; for vertices in different components the same pullback formulas and comparison lemmas still apply to empty fibers.
